photos.title: IPDB 6416 image 13, 'Whitewood Playfield'
photos.notes: A near top-down photograph of a whitewood playfield fitted in a cabinet; every position is read on it after rectification.

photos.title: Pinside gallery image 'RobZombie_Playfield (resized)'
photos.notes: A lit production playfield photographed from the front, mapped onto the whitewood by a 32-point homography (RMS 3.2 px); it names each insert and part and supplies the inserts the whitewood lacks.

rzspook.method: The whitewood photograph is corrected for barrel distortion (one radial term) and rectified onto a 952 x 2185 frame at playfield level. The left and right edges are measured where the bare wood meets the cabinet walls (the right edge is the shooter lane floor's outer edge). The main playfield's rear edge is hidden under the upper playfield and its front end under the apron, so those two lines come from a parallax estimate based on the wall tops, with the camera's foot placed at the front wall; that leaves a uniform uncertainty of about 45 px (2 percent of the length) in y, and the measured side edges are not quite parallel, so a position can be off by up to a few percent near the rear. Raised parts are not placed: parallax displaces them.

photos.title: Pinside gallery image of a production Jetsons cabinet from above
photos.notes: A production cabinet photographed from above and slightly in front; the playfield artwork names every insert, and every position is read on it after rectification.

jetsons.method: The photograph is corrected for barrel distortion (one radial term) and rectified onto a 952 x 2185 frame at playfield level: the left edge where the side wall meets the playfield, the right edge at the shooter lane wall's base (seen only in the front half and extended to the rear), the rear edge where the back wall meets the playfield, and the apron's lower edge as the front reference (the apron stands about two inches above the playfield). The side lines are not quite parallel and the flipper pivots' midpoint sits 12 px left of the centre line, so a position can be off by a few percent, most near the right rear. Raised parts are not placed: parallax displaces them.
